anu (docs): quick bug: linkcheck flagged non-unique fragment ids on a few pages after we flattened some nested guides. Example: two sections ended up with `#configuration` and the second occurrence gets dropped in the HTML, so sidebar links point to nothing.
ben (eng): ah, duplicate heading slugs. Did the build warn about duplicate ids?
link-bot: Warning: duplicate fragment id `configuration` found in /guides/setup.html (line ~120) and /guides/setup.html (line ~420).
anu (docs): yep. It only appears on pages where we collapsed subfolders into a single flat file; headings that were previously scoped by file now collide.
ben (eng): short-term: we can post-process and namespace in-page ids by prefixing with the top-level section, e.g. `#setup-configuration`. Could do a small script to rewrite headings without explicit ids.
anu (docs): that would be great. I'd prefer we avoid manually editing content everywhere. Also we should add a CI assertion to fail when duplicate fragment ids are detected in built HTML.
ben (eng): agreed. I'll open a tiny PR that adds the script and the CI check (linkcheck extension). The script will run only during build and will add prefixes based on the nearest H1.
ci-bot: job queued: docs/unique-fragment-guard (job #722).
anu (docs): thanks — when you open the PR please include a short README for the rule and a revert plan in case any external anchors break. We'll also run a quick smoke after merge to validate third-party links.
ben (eng): will do. PR incoming and assigning @anu for review.
